title: Post-Quantum Ratchet Messaging Under Application Stalls: An SPQR Study of Acknowledgment Policies and Receiver Buffer Limits
content: Application stalls can delay a messaging ratchet even when the receiving endpoint can authenticate and store ciphertexts. We study this interaction in a wrapper around a pinned Signal Sparse Post-Quantum Ratchet implementation. Acceptance-gated acknowledgments follow local application acceptance; durable-reception acknowledgments follow committed receiver custody. These are different delivery contracts. The wrapper combines immutable ciphertext retries, bounded sender outboxes and finite receiver pending storage. We measure communication to a declared conditional recovery witness separately from delivery and workload completion. Four distinct completed settings use fewer bytes to the witness under durable reception but 0.038–0.303% more whole-workload bytes. A separate adverse case attains a witness before rejecting a delayed ciphertext outside the receiver’s retention window. At the primary cut, a recorded capacity classification matches 53/54 constrained observations, with one exception at a shifted stall phase. A phase-specific occupancy diagnostic matches 54/54 retrospectively, as consistency and adjacent-capacity evidence. These deterministic observations support an implementation-specific account of receipt, retry, storage and ratchet interactions. They establish neither earliest recovery nor a universal storage bound, physical power-loss durability or an end-to-end post-compromise-security theorem. The witness remains conditional on one-time committed-state disclosure followed by passive observation.
